source_row.rationale: Cor pulmonale refers to right-sided heart failure resulting from chronic pulmonary disease (such as severe COPD), in which increased pulmonary vascular resistance from lung disease places excessive strain on the right ventricle over time, eventually leading to signs of right-sided heart failure such as peripheral edema and jugular venous distention.
source_row.source_detail: Cor pulmonale is right-ventricular structural/functional impairment caused by pulmonary disease/pulmonary hypertension; COPD is a common cause; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A client with severe, long-standing COPD develops signs of right-sided heart failure, including peripheral edema and jugular venous distention, and a new nurse assumes these findings must point to a separate, unrelated kidney problem.
